title: Opinions & discussions
goal: Hold your own in a discussion: agree and disagree politely, say 'I don't think …', 'it depends', 'to be honest', weigh how likely something is (maybe, might, I'm sure), say what someone should have done — about prices, politics and cricket.
intro:
Pashtuns love a good argument. In the hujra, at the tea stall and in every family WhatsApp group, people debate cricket, prices, politics and who said what — loudly, with a lot of 'by God' and 'look here', and usually with a laugh at the end. Knowing how to disagree without giving offence, and how to make a point stick, is what lets you take part instead of just listening.

In this unit you'll learn the phrases for agreeing, disagreeing and softening; **'maybe / might'** (شايد، ښايي، کېدای شي + the subjunctive) and the other degrees of certainty; **'I don't think …'**; and **'should have …'** (بايد + participle + وای) — essential for every post-match analysis.

grammar.title: Maybe, might and how sure you are
grammar.body:
**شايد** (unit 17), **ښايي** and **کېدای شي** all mean 'maybe / might'. They are followed by the **subjunctive** — the perfective present for events, **وي** for 'be':

شايد نن نه **راشي** 'he might not come today'
ښايي ناروغ **وي** 'he might be ill'
کېدای شي (چې) سبا باران **وشي** 'it might rain tomorrow'

**Might have** (a guess about the past) = participle + **وي**: شايد کيلي مې په موټر کې پاتې **شوې وي** 'maybe I left the keys in the car'; ښايي هغه زما پيغام نه **وي ليدلی** 'maybe he hasn't seen my message'. Transitive verbs stay ergative.

**The certainty scale**, from sure to impossible:
**حتماً / خامخا** + future: حتماً به راشي 'he'll definitely come'
**يقين لرم چې** … 'I'm sure that …'
**ګمان کوم چې** / **زما ګمان دی چې** … 'I reckon …'
**شايد / ښايي / کېدای شي** … 'maybe …'
**زه فکر نه کوم چې** … 'I don't think …' (grammar 2)
**هېڅ امکان نشته چې** … 'there's no chance that …'

**The trap**: with a maybe-word about the future, don't use the ordinary present (راځي) or the future (به راشي) — use the bare subjunctive: شايد **راشي**.

grammar.title: 'I don't think …' — agreeing and disagreeing politely
grammar.body:
**'I don't think …'**: as in English, the negative goes on the thinking verb, and the چې-clause stays positive: **زه فکر نه کوم چې** هغه رښتيا وايي 'I don't think he's telling the truth'. For a future or possible event the clause takes the subjunctive: زه فکر نه کوم چې هغه **راشي**. You can also say **زما په فکر** … **نه** …: زما په فکر دا سمه **نه** ده.

**Agreeing**: حق په تا دی / حق لرې 'you're right' · بالکل 'exactly' · زه هم **همداسې** فکر کوم 'I think so too' · ښه ټکی دی 'good point' · ښکاره خبره ده 'obviously'.

**Disagreeing politely** — soften first, then disagree, usually with **خو** 'but':
ستا خبره سمه ده، **خو** … 'you have a point, but …'
بښنه غواړم، خو زما نظر بل دی 'sorry, but I see it differently'
**رښتيا ووايم** … 'to be honest …' (lit. let me speak the truth)
په دې کې درسره موافق نه يم 'I don't agree with you on this'
قانع نه شوم 'I'm not convinced'

**It depends**: **په** X **پورې اړه لري** 'it depends on X': دا په پيسو پورې اړه لري.

**Register**: with friends you can be blunt — نه ياره، غلطه ده! 'no mate, that's wrong!'. With elders, never say غلط to their face: say ستاسو خبره سمه ده، خو … and use تاسو.

examples.en: I don't think this plan will work.

examples.en: You're right, but there's another point as well. (polite)

examples.roman: dā pə hawā́ póre aṛa lari.

grammar.title: 'Should have …': بايد + participle + وای
grammar.body:
To say what someone **should have done** (and didn't), Pashto combines **بايد** with the past participle and **وای** — the same وای as the unreal conditions of unit 19:

بايد زه وختي **راغلی وای** 'I should have come early'
بايد تا ما ته **ويلي وای** 'you should have told me'

The usual rules apply:
• **Intransitive** verbs: the participle agrees with the subject: بايد ته **راغلی** وای (man) / **راغلې** وای (woman).
• **Transitive** verbs are **ergative**: the doer is ما، تا، هغه، موږ …, and the participle agrees with the **object**: بايد موږ دا ميچ **ګټلی** وای (ميچ m sg), بايد ما ټکټونه **اخيستي** وای (m pl), بايد تا دا خبره نه وای **کړې** (f). With no object, use **-i**: ويلي وای.
• **Shouldn't have**: put **نه** before وای: بايد دا خبره **نه وای** کړې.

This is the grammar of every post-match argument: بايد هغه دا ګول **وهلی وای**! 'he should have scored that!'.

Compare: بايد **ووايې** 'you must say' (subjunctive, still possible) vs بايد **ويلي وای** 'you should have said' (too late now).

lines.en: Prices are up, son. Tell the government!

lines.en: See, that's another argument you're not going to win!

culture: Arguing is a social sport among Pashtuns — in the **حجره**, at the tea stall, in the family WhatsApp group — and a heated discussion usually ends with tea and a joke, not hurt feelings. People back up their point with **په خدای** 'by God', **ګوره** 'look' and **رښتيا ووايم** 'honestly', and interrupting is normal. Two lines you shouldn't cross: don't contradict an **elder** bluntly in front of others (say ستاسو خبره سمه ده، خو … and let it go), and be careful with **politics** with people you don't know well — Afghan politics, the Taliban, Pakistan–Afghanistan relations and ethnic questions can turn a friendly chat sour fast. **Cricket** is the safe passion: the Afghan national team grew out of refugee camps around Peshawar to beat world champions, and its stars (Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi) are heroes on both sides of the border, while Peshawar fans follow **Peshawar Zalmi** in the PSL. Football is popular with the young, and complaining about **ګراني** — prices — is something everyone agrees on.

lessons.title: Agreeing and disagreeing

tip.title: 'I don't think …' and polite 'but'
tip.body:
- **زه فکر نه کوم چې** + clause: نه goes on فکر کوم; a possible event takes the subjunctive: … چې هغه **راشي**.
- Or: **زما په فکر** … **نه** ده.
- Soften, then disagree with **خو**: ستا خبره سمه ده، **خو** …
- Agree: حق په تا دی، زه هم همداسې فکر کوم.

lessons.title: Maybe, probably, definitely

tip.title: Maybe / might + subjunctive
tip.body:
- **شايد / ښايي / کېدای شي** + subjunctive: شايد نن نه **راشي**; ښايي ناروغ **وي**.
- Might have: participle + **وي**: شايد پاتې **شوې وي**.
- Surer: **يقين لرم چې**، **ګمان کوم چې**. No way: **هېڅ امکان نشته چې** … + subjunctive.
- Not راځي or به راشي after شايد.

sentences.native: زه د سياست په اړه خبرې نه کوم.
sentences.roman: zə də siyāsát pə aṛa xabə́re na kawə́m.
sentences.en: I don't talk about politics.

sentences.native: په دې ورځو کې ټول خلک د ګراني خبرې کوي.
sentences.roman: pə de wradzó ke ṭol xálək də grāní xabə́re kawí.
sentences.en: These days everyone is talking about prices.

sentences.native: ګراني ډېره شوې ده، ډوډۍ هم ګرانه ده.
sentences.roman: grāní ḍéra shə́we da, ḍoḍə́y ham grā́na da.
sentences.en: Prices have shot up — even bread is expensive.

sentences.native: حکومت بايد څه وکړي.
sentences.roman: hukumát bāyád tsə wə́kṛi.
sentences.en: The government should do something.

sentences.native: په حکومت باور نه لرم.
sentences.roman: pə hukumát bāwár na lárəm.
sentences.en: I don't trust the government.

sentences.native: ټاکنې کله دي؟
sentences.roman: ṭākəné kə́la di?
sentences.en: When are the elections?

sentences.native: ته به په ټاکنو کې ګډون وکړې؟
sentences.roman: tə ba pə ṭākəno ke gaḍún wə́kṛe?
sentences.en: Are you going to vote in the elections? (lit. take part)

sentences.native: نن دې ورځپاڼه لوستې ده؟
sentences.roman: nən de wradzpā́ṇa lwasté da?
sentences.en: Have you read today's paper?

sentences.native: اوس څوک ورځپاڼه لولي؟ ټول خبرونه په ټيلفون کې دي.
sentences.roman: os tsok wradzpā́ṇa lwalí? ṭol xabarúna pə ṭelifún ke di.
sentences.en: Who reads newspapers now? All the news is on your phone.

sentences.native: د ځوانانو لپاره دنده پيدا کول ډېر سخت دي.
sentences.roman: də dzwānā́no lapā́ra dánda paydā́ kawə́l ḍer saxt di.
sentences.en: Finding a job is really hard for young people.

lessons.title: Cricket, football — and what they should have done

tip.title: 'Should have': بايد + participle + وای
tip.body:
- بايد + participle + **وای**: بايد زه وختي **راغلی وای**.
- Transitive = ergative, participle agrees with the object: بايد موږ ميچ **ګټلی** وای; no object → **-i**: ويلي وای.
- Shouldn't have: **نه وای**.
- Compare بايد **ووايې** 'you must say' (still possible).

new: بايد تا ما ته ويلي وای.

sentences.native: بايد موږ دا ميچ ګټلی وای.
sentences.roman: bāyád muẓ dā mich gaṭə́lay wāy.
sentences.en: We should have won this match.

sentences.native: بايد احمد هغه ګول وهلی وای!
sentences.roman: bāyád ahmád haġá gol wahə́lay wāy!
sentences.en: He should have scored that goal!

sentences.native: بايد زه وختي راغلی وای.
sentences.roman: bāyád zə waxtí rāġə́lay wāy.
sentences.en: I should have come early.

sentences.native: بايد تا ټکټ مخکې اخيستی وای.
sentences.roman: bāyád tā ṭikáṭ mə́xke axistáy wāy.
sentences.en: You should have bought the ticket in advance.

sentences.native: تا بايد هغه ته دا خبره نه وای کړې.
sentences.roman: tā bāyád haġə́ ta dā xabə́ra na wāy kṛe.
sentences.en: You shouldn't have told him that.

sentences.native: بايد ما هغه ته زنګ وهلی وای.
sentences.roman: bāyád mā haġə́ ta zang wahə́lay wāy.
sentences.en: I should have called him.

sentences.native: بايد ته هم راغلی وای، ميچ ډېر ښه و.
sentences.roman: bāyád tə ham rāġə́lay wāy, mich ḍer ṣə wə.
sentences.en: You should have come too — it was a great match.

sentences.native: بايد ما د ميچ ټکټونه اخيستي وای.
sentences.roman: bāyád mā də mich ṭikaṭúna axistí wāy.
sentences.en: I should have bought tickets for the match.

sentences.native: ميچ مساوي شو، يو يو.
sentences.roman: mich musāwí shu, yaw yaw.
sentences.en: The match was a draw, one all.

sentences.native: ته کرکټ خوښوې که فوټبال؟
sentences.roman: tə krikáṭ xwaṣawé ka fuṭbā́l?
sentences.en: Do you like cricket or football?

sentences.native: زموږ ملي ټيم ډېر ښه لوبه کوي.
sentences.roman: zmuẓ milí ṭim ḍer ṣa lóba kawí.
sentences.en: Our national team plays really well.

sentences.native: نن شپه ميچ دی، راځې چې يو ځای يې وګورو؟
sentences.roman: nən shpa mich day, rā́dze che yaw dzāy ye wə́goru?
sentences.en: There's a match tonight — want to watch it together?
